audit.why: 50.22% over 227 games, EVEN, 4/10. Camille owns levels 1-5, level 6 is the skill window, and Sejuani reclaims the lane on two tank items. This matches the already-audited mirror at audits/top/sejuani__camille.json, which states the same split from her side.

Spike ladder is right: Camille's level 2-3 Hookshot plus Precision Protocol recast, level 6 Hextech Ultimatum, first-item bruiser peak; Sejuani's payoff is her second tank item and Glacial Prison. No power shift is invented, and the level chart already agrees with the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup never names a single Sejuani ability — she has 'her W chip', 'her E stun', 'her R', 'her Q dash' throughout. The packet flags exactly this. Camille's own abilities are mostly unnamed too.
audit.why: Riot's names are Fury of the North (P), Arctic Assault (Q), Winter's Wrath (W), Permafrost (E) and Glacial Prison (R). The decisive interaction is that Permafrost is a 1.5s detonator, not a stun on demand — it needs two Frost stacks applied by Arctic Assault, Winter's Wrath or autos first. That is the real gate on every trade, and Arctic Assault at 18s against Hookshot at 16s is why Camille dictates the engage. Glacial Prison also out-ranges the Hextech Ultimatum 1300 to 475, but Camille is untargetable through the R dash, so a stun spent into the leap is wasted — the mirror already ships that fact from Sejuani's side.
audit.corrected: All five Sejuani abilities named; the two-Frost-stack gate on Permafrost stated; Arctic Assault 18s vs Hookshot 16s and the Glacial Prison range/untargetability interaction written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: full winCon says 'punish his Permafrost cooldown' — wrong gender, and wrong mechanic: Permafrost is a 1.5s cooldown, so there is no cooldown to punish.
audit.why: Permafrost fires whenever two Frost stacks are on you; the punishable resource is the stacks and Arctic Assault's 18s, not the E cooldown. Advising a player to wait out a 1.5s cooldown is advice that gets them stunned.
audit.corrected: winCon now tells you to fight her below two Frost stacks.

audit.why: The stated mistake — treating level 6 as a free kill because the R isolates her — is the right one and matches the win-rate flatness at that stage.

edits.before: Her tank body and your single ability both lack kill pressure at level 1 — just last-hit and avoid her W chip.
edits.after: Fury of the North armours her and you have one ability — no kill threat, so last-hit and stay out of Winter's Wrath.

edits.before: Your second point unlocks the Q recast's bonus true damage, which beats her flat tank stats before she's even stacked the two Frosts her E stun needs.
edits.after: Your Precision Protocol recast lands bonus true damage through her tank stats before she has the two Frost stacks that Permafrost (E) needs to stun you.

edits.before: It's even at 6 — your R isolates her out of her teamfight role, but her R root and bigger tank body answer your all-in.
edits.after: Even at 6 — The Hextech Ultimatum strips her teamfight role, but Glacial Prison roots you and her tank body answers your all-in.

edits.before: Once you have Q and a point in W you out-trade her — the Q recast's bonus true damage ignores her tank stats, and she can't punish back until she's stacked two Frosts (Q/W/autos) to detonate her E stun.
edits.after: Once you have Q and a point in W you out-trade her — the Precision Protocol recast's true damage ignores her tank stats, and she can't punish until Arctic Assault or Winter's Wrath stacks two Frosts for Permafrost.

edits.before: Your R drags her into an isolated 1v1 where her teamfight value evaporates, but her R roots you on the projectile hit and she's tankier — respect that this stage is even, not a free kill.
edits.after: The Hextech Ultimatum drags her into a 1v1 where her teamfight value evaporates — and you are untargetable through the dash, so a Glacial Prison spent into it is wasted. She still out-bulks you here.

edits.before: "Sejuani's level 1 is a sturdy tank body with no kill threat, and you only have one ability, so this stage is a wash — just last-hit and don't eat free W chip. The lane swings your way at 2-3: your Q recast true damage and W's outer-edge max-HP slash chew through her starting tank stats faster than her chip hurts you, and your Adaptive Defense shield eats the first hit of any trade she starts. Crucially, her E stun isn't on demand — she has to land two Frost stacks (Q, W, or autos) before she can detonate it, so trade while she's under two stacks, E in, W-pull, and recast Q before she can lock you down — she has no dash to escape yours."
edits.after: "Sejuani's level 1 is a sturdy tank body with no kill threat, and you only have one ability, so this stage is a wash — last-hit and don't eat free Winter's Wrath chip. The lane swings your way at 2-3: Precision Protocol's recast true damage and the Tactical Sweep outer edge chew through her starting tank stats faster than her chip hurts you, and your Adaptive Defenses shield eats the first hit of any trade she starts. Crucially, Permafrost is not a stun on demand — she needs two Frost stacks from Arctic Assault, Winter's Wrath or autos first, so trade below two stacks. Her Arctic Assault is 18s to your 16s Hookshot, so you get the engage."

edits.before: Shred her with true damage and bully her weak 1v1. Keep the wave playable, punish his Permafrost cooldown, and never throw the lane by over-extending your Hookshot.
edits.after: Shred her with true damage and bully her weak 1v1. Keep the wave playable, fight her below two Frost stacks, and never throw the lane by over-extending your Hookshot.

notes: Mirror at audits/top/sejuani__camille.json was reused for the Glacial Prison 1300 vs Hextech Ultimatum 475 range fact and the untargetable-through-the-dash call; both directions now state the same thing from opposite sides and the level charts already agree (Camille 0-3 and 5-6, Skill at 4). _missing-interactions.json wants a line saying Sejuani cancels Camille's R 'channel' — Riot's description for The Hextech Ultimatum is a dash to a target with no channel, so that generated line is a derived-flag misfire and I did not write it.
